summary: Verified frontend webpack/is-plain-obj hotfix. Loaded the app root URL via the public REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL - the page returned HTTP 200, title 'BotSmith | AI Agent Builder For Colleges & Universities' rendered, and there was NO 'Compiled with problems' overlay, NO 'Module build failed' text, and NO console errors referencing 'is-plain-obj', 'unified', 'Module build failed' or webpack module resolution. /var/log/supervisor/frontend.out.log shows repeated 'Compiled successfully! / webpack compiled successfully' with zero errors after the supervisor restart. The AI assistant widget rendered in the bottom-right, confirming React app mounted and hydrated. Hotfix is confirmed working.

integration_issues.issue: POST /api/admin/direct-login/generate-token/admin-001 returned HTTP 403 Forbidden - could not use the documented bypass to reach /dashboard for a deeper smoke test. This is unrelated to the webpack hotfix scope but worth flagging (endpoint may now require auth or admin id changed).

action_items: Hotfix verified - no action needed for the is-plain-obj/unified compile error.
Optional: investigate why /api/admin/direct-login/generate-token/admin-001 now returns 403 (may block future UI testing that relies on the direct-login bypass).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Frontend compiles cleanly after the supervisor restart. If future runs re-see the ENOENT/is-plain-obj error, first check /var/log/supervisor/frontend.out.log and try `sudo supervisorctl restart frontend` before touching node_modules. Direct-login token endpoint currently returns 403 - for UI-authenticated tests, get updated credentials/route from main agent.
rca of the issue: Stale webpack-dev-server process cached a resolution path to nested node_modules/unified/node_modules/is-plain-obj that no longer existed on disk. Every hot-reload recompile kept using the cached (invalid) path -> ENOENT. Restarting the frontend supervisor process forced webpack to re-resolve modules from scratch against the current (correct) node_modules tree, resolving the compile error. Verified post-restart via supervisor logs and browser load.
